title: "Methods"

## Study Design

This is a systematic review and Bayesian meta-analysis of studies comparing post-transplant cyclophosphamide (PTCy) to alternative GVHD prophylaxis regimens in allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation. The extraction database comprises 220 studies (457 arms, 10 RCTs) drawn from 9 extraction blocks, with 190 papers excluded per PRISMA criteria. Three pre-specified comparisons were analysed:

- **Comparison 1:** PTCy vs CNI+MTX/MMF-based prophylaxis
- **Comparison 2:** PTCy vs ATG-based prophylaxis
- **Comparison 3:** Within-PTCy dose/schedule variants (new in Block 9 expansion)

## Outcomes

Ten outcomes were evaluated across transplant, GVHD, and infection domains:

| Outcome | Definition | Timepoint preference |
|---|---|---|
| Overall survival (OS) | All-cause mortality | 2yr > 1yr > EoF |
| Non-relapse mortality (NRM) | Death without prior relapse | 2yr > 1yr > EoF |
| Relapse-related mortality (RRM) | Death with or after relapse | 2yr > 1yr > EoF |
| aGVHD grade II–IV | Acute GVHD by consensus criteria | D+100 > D+180 > EoF |
| cGVHD moderate-severe (NIH) | Chronic GVHD by NIH severity grading | 1yr > 2yr > EoF |
| CMV any-reactivation | Any CMV reactivation by PCR/antigenemia | D+100 > D+180 > EoF > 1yr |
| BK virus reactivation | BK viruria/viremia or haemorrhagic cystitis | D+100 > D+180 > EoF |
| BSI (any pathogen) | Positive blood culture | D+100 > D+180 > EoF |
| IFI (any) | Proven/probable invasive fungal infection | D+100 > D+180 > EoF > 1yr |
| Infection-related mortality (IRM) | Death attributed to infection | EoF > 1yr > 2yr |

## Statistical Framework

### Bayesian Random-Effects Models

All models were fit using `brms` with the `rstan` backend. The general form:

$$
\text{events}_i \mid \text{trials}_i \sim \text{Binomial}(\pi_i)
$$
$$
\text{logit}(\pi_i) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot \text{PTCy}_i + \beta_2 \cdot \text{tp\_early}_i + u_{j[i]}
$$
$$
u_j \sim \text{Normal}(0, \tau)
$$

### Prior Specification

| Parameter | Prior | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| $$\beta_{\text{PTCy}}$$ | Normal(0, 2.5) | Weakly informative; 95% prior mass covers OR 0.007–140 |
| $$\beta_{\text{tp\_early}}$$ | Normal(0, 2.5) | Timepoint adjustment; same prior class |
| Intercept | Normal(0, 1.5) | Baseline event rate |
| $$\tau$$ | Student-t(3, 0, 1) | Heterogeneity; weakly informative with heavy tails for sparse outcomes |

### Model Hierarchy

- **M1 (Direct effect):** PTCy + timepoint adjustment + random study intercept
- **M2 (Steroid-adjusted):** M1 + arm-level systemic steroid exposure (% receiving steroids for GVHD). Post-Block-9 M2 models use complete-case analysis (arms with missing steroid data excluded).
- **M3 (aGVHD-adjusted, CMV only):** M1 + arm-level aGVHD grade II–IV cumulative incidence

### MCMC Configuration

- 4 chains × 4,000 iterations (1,000 warmup + 3,000 sampling) = 12,000 posterior draws
- Convergence assessed via R̂ (all ≤ 1.005) and effective sample sizes (bulk ESS, tail ESS)
- No divergent transitions in any fitted model

### Frequentist Comparison

All Bayesian models were cross-checked with frequentist random-effects models (REML) via `metafor` (v5.0-1) using log-OR as the effect size. BSI in Comparison 2 (k = 3) was pooled using Mantel-Haenszel fixed-effect estimation.

## Arm Classification

### Comparison 1
Arms were classified as PTCy if `ptcy_used == "Y"` and as control if the primary prophylaxis was CNI+MTX or CNI+MMF without PTCy.

### Comparison 2
- **Primary analysis:** Clean binary — PTCy-only (`ptcy_used == "Y"`, `atg_used == "N"`) vs ATG-only (`ptcy_used == "N"`, `atg_used == "Y"`)
- **Sensitivity analysis:** PTCy+ATG combination arms reclassified as PTCy-side; mixed-ATG arms classified by PTCy co-administration; "neither" arms excluded

## GRADE Assessment

Certainty of evidence was assessed per the GRADE Handbook (Schünemann et al.) adapted for Bayesian meta-analyses of observational studies. Starting certainty: LOW. Cross-comparison coherence was considered as a potential upgrade criterion where applicable.
